# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 2 (Bu-Vb Np2)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np2
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 2
**Title (English, from literature):** Staying apart from one’s robes
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Udosita-sikkhāpada* constitutes the second rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* (relinquishment with expiation) section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. According to the rule, a monk who remains apart from any of his three prescribed robes for more than one day is required to forfeit the robe and confess the infraction. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case analysis has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Automated cross-linguistic alignments from DharmaNexus confirm close textual correspondences with Tibetan Vinaya literature, notably the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus].

Within the Pali corpus, DharmaNexus detects extensive textual reuse (1,725 matches across 123 texts) [DharmaNexus]. The text shares significant phrasing with canonical Khandhaka treatises—such as the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15), *Samuccayakkhandhaka* (Kd 13), *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11), and *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14)—as well as sibling Vibhaṅga rules including Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1, 3, and 14 [DharmaNexus]. It is also extensively cited and glossed in post-canonical exegetical and manual literature, prominently the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā*, *Khuddasikkhā-mūlasikkhā*, *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
